title: Costs rebuild 2 · piece 2: runner posts per-request records for claude-code (snapshots still posted)
description:
**Piece 2 of LIN-4195** (runner, simple-dispatcher). It covers D9–D11. Harbour piece 1 must be deployed first. During this window the read does not change, so figures do not change and records accumulate for piece 3.

**Walk (D9):**

* At each flush, walk the transcript(s) into per-request records: per-field max within a `message.id`, as `walkUsage` does today (LIN-3229). Skip `<synthetic>` and all-zero messages.
* **Review note 8:** for a line without `message.id`, fall back to the line's top-level `requestId`. If both are absent, skip the line and count the skip in the oplog. Never post a synthetic per-line id.
* The walk must reproduce piece 0's records JSON exactly.

**Ledger and resend (D9):**

* Keep a per-session ledger `{requestId: fingerprint}`.
* Post what is new or changed, in batches of 100.
* A batch enters the ledger only on a 200, committed via `updateState` (the LIN-459 rule).
* Per-record `rejected` is permanent: log it and do not retry. A 5xx, timeout or 404 means nothing was acknowledged: retry at the next flush.
* **Review note 6:** keep the ledger compact (one short hash per id) or in a per-session side file. `state/sessions.json` is already 1.58 MB for 141 sessions and is rewritten on every `updateState`. Correctness must never depend on the ledger.

**Flush points (D10, absorbs LIN-3948):**

* Create one flush function, called from three places:
  * (a) Stop: it replaces the seven `if (WORKER_USAGE_RELAY) await postUsageSnapshot(...)` sites in `hook.js` with one call. `postUsageSnapshot` itself **stays** in this piece; piece 6 removes it;
  * (b) the terminal-session cleanup/reap;
  * (c) the cancel/abort path in `reapers.js`/`dispatcher.js`.
* (b) and (c) read `session.transcriptPath`, which the hook stores (\~`hook.js:1771`), with `locateTranscript(sessionId)` as the fallback.
* **Review note 7:** run the reap flush at the terminal transition, not at the 7-day record pass.

**Subagents (D11, absorbs LIN-3859's subagent half):**

* Also walk `<session-dir>/<session-id>/subagents/agent-*.jsonl`, with `agent` set to the subagent id. Re-check the layout on the runner host before coding.
* A message id present in both the main and a subagent file is one request.
* Replace the stale comment and test that say sidechain lines sit in the main transcript. At HEAD they are `transcript.js:432-435` (the plan cited :411-414) and `test/transcript.test.js:488`. Keep `isSidechain` lines counted when they do appear in the main file: dedupe by id across files, never by file.

**Witnesses:**

* Fault injection: the server returns 500 for the second of three batches. The ledger keeps that batch unacknowledged, the next flush sends it, and the final server-side sum equals the oracle.
* After deleting the ledger, a full re-send leaves the sum unchanged.
* A message id shared between the main and a subagent file is posted as one request.
* A tail that is missing at Stop and present at reap is held after the reap flush. This must fail with Stop-only posting.
* **Review note 11:** the records sum to the oracle for every piece-0 case. Keep this alongside the intake rejection test; it is what proves the runner never posts running totals.

**Acceptance:**

* The witnesses above pass.
* Snapshot posting is unchanged.
* The oplog shows record posts, plus counts of rejects and skips.
* Use the existing shared Stop-hook test driver (LIN-4183).

---

**Parent:** LIN-4195 "Costs rebuild 2: one record per model request, summed". Its full design (decisions D1–D14, the replay change list, the witnesses, the order of landing) is in LIN-4195's description under "## Implementation Plan". The plan-review notes are in LIN-4195's comment `eedab867-0fe0-4b15-b74a-2b78240f11d1`. The numbered notes cited here ("review note N") refer to that comment.

Session fit: fits one session
Plan-review due: no — covered by LIN-4195's approving plan-review (comment eedab867-0fe0-4b15-b74a-2b78240f11d1, rev 1)
Grounding commits: Harbour (JKershaw/LinearViewer) `72305215`, runner (JKershaw/simple-dispatcher) `cc2650a`. At breakdown (2026-11-04 \~01:45Z) neither repo had a commit after these.

The parent's approved plan is this piece's starting point; read it in full in LIN-4195's description. Follow it. Where the code shows it is wrong, change course and say so on LIN-4195.

---

## Implemented (close-out)

Merged as [https://github.com/JKershaw/simple-dispatcher/pull/314](<https://github.com/JKershaw/simple-dispatcher/pull/314>) (squash `9478e1c`). The plan in LIN-4195 was implemented as approved, with one correction: the walk also reads workflow subagent transcripts (`subagents/workflows/wf_*/agent-*.jsonl`), not only `subagents/agent-*.jsonl`. Nothing in this description was a discharged stage artifact, so the spec and acceptance above are kept unchanged. The full pre-close description is preserved in the task snapshots; the review and close-out are in the comment trail.

comments.body:
**Note from LIN-4197 review (piece 0, now merged): two tests piece 2's walk must carry.**

Piece 0's `request-records.json` (runner PR #312, merged as `b6fc9ab`) is correct, but it cannot prove two of the walk rules, because the fixture data never exercises them. In review, two mutations of the test-local walk (`test/helpers/transcript-corpus-walk.js`) left all 14 corpus tests green:
- per-field max replaced by "last line wins";
- the `<synthetic>` skip removed.

Why they survive: every streamed message id's lines only grow (including the main and subagent copies of `msg_sm_shared`, 50 → 120), and the only `<synthetic>` line is also all-zero, so the all-zero rule skips it anyway. A piece-2 walk that used last-wins, or skipped only all-zero messages, would still reproduce the file exactly.

So matching `request-records.json` is necessary but not sufficient. Piece 2's own tests must also include:
1. A message id whose later line carries a *smaller* field value than an earlier one (e.g. the main copy streams further than the subagent copy, or lines arrive non-monotone). The record must hold the per-field max.
2. A `<synthetic>` message with non-zero usage. It must produce no record.

Acceptance: both cases fail against a last-wins walk and against an all-zero-only skip.

**Note from LIN-4198 (piece 1, merged and deployed) — producer contract for the runner side.**

The intake (`POST /api/proxy/runner/usage/:id`, twin `POST /api/dispatch/usage/:itemId`) only accepts posts while the dispatch row is `status:'taken'` AND taken by the posting token (the feedback ownership rule). So the runner must:
- post every usage batch inside that window, including the final batch around the terminal `[done]` marker (post it *before* the row is closed);
- treat a `404` as "not yours / no longer taken" and stop retrying that batch;
- send at most 100 records per call; a record over 2,000,000 prompt tokens, with a negative/non-finite field, an over-long id or no `requestId` is rejected per record (`{rejected:[{requestId, reason}]}`), and an all-zero-token record is reported as applied but not stored.
- the dispatch route refuses the single-use Harbour OS feedback token (401, not spent); the runner twin uses the proxy token with the `take` grant.
Reposting the same `requestId` is safe: tokens and `costUsd` are `$max`-merged, identity is `$setOnInsert`.

**LIN-4199 (piece 2): PR ready for review: https://github.com/JKershaw/simple-dispatcher/pull/314**

Branch `feat/lin-4199-runner-request-records`, head `ff94a7f` (one feature commit `7de98ce` plus a CI harness fix `ff94a7f`). Not merged; left for review.

**What changed.** The runner walks each claude-code transcript (main file and `subagents/agent-*.jsonl`) into one record per request and posts them to `/api/dispatch/usage/:itemId` in batches of at most 100, alongside the unchanged snapshots. Flush points: Stop (one awaited call before the turn's feedback, deadline-bounded, fail-open), done-window reap, stall-failsafe FAILED, `failSession`, forced-resume cancel, and `applyAbortEffects` (manual abort and halt sweep). Opencode and fast-fail sites are not wired, with reasons in the PR table.

**Evidence.**
- Local full suite (macOS): 3961 tests, 3956 pass, 0 fail, 5 skipped.
- CI `unit tests` (run 41775320823): SUCCESS. Its totals are 3947 tests, 3940 pass, 0 fail, 7 skipped. The counts differ by platform; I have not reconciled every test.
- The first CI run was red because of a test-harness issue (a fake hung POST drained the Linux event loop). Fixed in `ff94a7f` with no assertion changed.
- Pre-existing assertions are unchanged; the diff removes four lines in existing test files (documented in the PR). `postUsageSnapshot` call sites are unchanged (7).
- Mutation checks on 9 guards and wirings; each named witness fails when its guard is broken.

**Decisions.**
- Only a 200 acknowledges a batch. A `rejected` record is permanent and enters the ledger.
- A failed batch does not stop later batches.
- The ledger is compact (request id plus 12-hex fingerprint) and is not pruned. Correctness never depends on it.

**Cancel acceptance.** Code-proven, not tested end-to-end against live Harbour. A cancelled `taken` row keeps status `taken` (`dispatch-store.js:1566`, and no abort path writes status), so the intake does not 404.

**Limits.** A permanent 400 retries on every flush (visible in the oplog). Harbour's intake was not run live. The reap seam covers only COMPLETED with `closeOnDone` and a window. Piece 3 (measurement) and piece 4 (read switch) are not included.

Left In Progress for review and close-out.

**Autopilot (stepper) run summary — LIN-4199 implementation arc**

Beats run in one warm session (root dispatch `19a8850c-70ed-42c1-aa14-c741691e6880`), all kind `implementation`:
1. **Ground + red witnesses** — branch `feat/lin-4199-runner-request-records`; 31 witnesses red for the right reason; pre-change baseline 0 failures.
2. **Walker + ledger/resend flush** — pure walk reproduces `request-records.json`; per-field max, `<synthetic>`/all-zero skips, requestId fallback with counted skips; 100-record batches, 200-only acknowledgement via `updateState`. Challenge: auth contract and exact failure count reconciled.
3. **Wiring (Stop / reap / cancel), subagents, stale comments, mutation proof** — then a **corrective** beat 3 after I challenged two gaps the worker had listed (only the done-window reap was wired; cancel acceptance unproven). Result: stall, `failSession` and forced-resume-cancel seams wired with real-seam witnesses; cancel verdict cited (a cancelled `taken` row keeps status `taken`).
4. **Push, PR, CI, Linear** — PR #314.

**Evidence (verified by me, not taken from the worker's report):** https://github.com/JKershaw/simple-dispatcher/pull/314 open against `main`, head `ff94a7f`; CI check `unit tests` SUCCESS on that head (run 41775320823); the earlier red run was a test-harness event-loop issue, fixed without changing any assertion. Local full suite 3956 pass / 0 fail / 5 skipped.

**What holds / what review should look at:** the LIN-4197 mutation-gap witnesses (non-monotone max, non-zero `<synthetic>`); 404 handling — the LIN-4198 note says to stop retrying a 404'd batch while this ticket's constraint says treat 404 as nothing acknowledged and retry at the next flush; the code follows the ticket constraint, reviewer should confirm that is the intended reading; cancel acceptance is code-proven only (not run against live Harbour); a permanent 400 would retry every flush; reap covers COMPLETED+closeOnDone+window only (opencode is piece 5, fast-fail has no transcript).

**Left:** independent `review`, then `close-out` (merge, Done). Not merged; LIN-4199 stays In Progress.

## Review — LIN-4199

Reviewed PR https://github.com/JKershaw/simple-dispatcher/pull/314, head `ff94a7f` (base `b6fc9ab`).

CI: green. The `unit tests` check passed on `ff94a7f` (run 41775320823). I re-ran the suite locally on the same head: 3961 tests, 3956 pass, 0 fail, 5 skipped.

### Scope vs plan
The diff covers D9–D11 as planned:
- the pure walk and ledger (`request-usage.js`);
- the flush (`request-usage-flush.js`);
- one Stop call in `hook.js`;
- reap, stall, `failSession`, forced-resume cancel and `applyAbortEffects` seams;
- stale comment and test fixes at `transcript.js:432` and `test/transcript.test.js:488`.

The implementation stayed inside the plan's files. Snapshot posting is unchanged: `await postUsageSnapshot(` appears 7 times in `hook.js` on both main and the PR. `detectClaudeCodeLane` moved, unchanged, into the pure module.

Regression check:
- `git log -30` on `hook.js`, `reapers.js`, `dispatcher.js`, `transcript.js`, `config.js` and `feedback.js` shows no revert or re-applied fix.
- LIN-4172 (the reap split into 24 h clone and 7 d record passes) is respected. The reap flush sits in `reapDoneSessionWindows` at the terminal transition, not in the 7-day record pass (review note 7).
- No commits landed on main after the grounding commit except `b6fc9ab` (piece 0), which is this PR's base.

### Harbour contract, checked at LinearViewer `9cc5ff9c`
- `routes/dispatch.js:1668` uses `feedbackLimiter` and `authenticateDispatchToken`. The runner posts there with `getTokenForWorkspace`, which is correct.
- `lib/request-usage-intake.js` matches the wire shape the runner sends. `lane`, `agent` and `effort` are strings or null, `costUsd` is null, `at` is an ISO string, and there are at most 100 records per call.
- The cancel claim holds. `readTakenForUsage` filters on `status:'taken'`. `'cancelled'` is written only for queued rows (`dispatch-store.js:1508`), and a taken row stays `taken`. So reap, stall and cancel posts are not refused with a 404.

### Mutation checks (each reverted afterwards)
I broke each guard or wiring below and ran `test/request-usage-*.test.js` plus `transcript.test.js`. Every mutation turned the named witness red:
- last-wins in place of per-field max: 2 fail (witness b)
- `<synthetic>` skip removed: 1 fail (witness c)
- `requestId` fallback removed: 1 fail (witness e)
- any status acknowledges: 3 fail (500, timeout, 404)
- all-zero skip removed: corpus `synthetic-tail` and witness d fail
- subagent walk removed: witness g fails
- `transcriptPath` ignored: 18 fail
- one fail per seam with that seam's wiring removed: reap, stall, cancel (2), `failSession`, forced-resume
- Stop wiring removed: 9 fail
- deadline guard removed: 2 fail

The LIN-4197 mutation-gap cases (a non-monotone max and a non-zero `<synthetic>` message) are present and do their job. The corpus test deep-equals `request-records.json` for every piece-0 case, so the records sum to the oracle (review note 11).

### Isolated, or one of a class?
The class is billed sub-agent transcripts outside the main file (D11). On the runner host (`~/.claude/projects`), sub-agent transcripts sit in two layouts:
- `<sid>/subagents/agent-*.jsonl`: 37 files, walked.
- `<sid>/subagents/workflows/wf_*/agent-*.jsonl`: 36 files, **not walked**. These are Workflow-tool agents, beside a `journal.jsonl`.

The workflow files carry billed assistant usage. For example, `msg_011CdUANrTzMB6ePkgB8tfB5` on `claude-fable-5` has `isSidechain:true` and 24,827 cache-creation tokens. `subagentSources` reads only the top level of `subagents/`, so that spend is never posted. No dispatched workspace on this host has run a workflow yet, but dispatched sessions do have the Workflow tool. This instance is **inside**, under D11's sub-agent class, and is ledger item 1. The plan's path (`subagents/agent-*.jsonl`) was incomplete, and close-out should note that on LIN-4195.

Opencode and runner-kit are **outside**: piece 5 (LIN-4202) owns them. Fast-fail sites have no transcript.

### What CI Did Not Prove
1. **Workflow sub-agent transcripts are not walked.** **Inside** (D11, sub-agent transcripts; the walk must cover all billed sub-agent files).
   - Settle **before the merge**. In `request-usage-flush.js` `subagentSources`, also read `subagents/workflows/*/agent-*.jsonl`.
   - Order: top-level files first, then workflow directories, both sorted. `agent` is the file's basename. `journal.jsonl` and `*.meta.json` are not read.
   - Add a witness to `test/request-usage-stop.test.js`: an id present only in `<transcript>/subagents/workflows/wf_x/agent-b.jsonl` is posted with `agent:'agent-b'`, and an id shared with the main file is posted once at the per-field max.
   - The condition that tells right from wrong: the witness is red with the workflows read removed and green with it.
   - Update the `transcript.js:432` comment to name both locations.
2. **Live intake acceptance.** The consumer dispatch token is accepted on `/api/dispatch/usage/:itemId`, and the real 200 body is `{applied, rejected}`. **Inside**: this change depends on it. CI used a fake server.
   - Settle **after the deploy**. For the first dispatched claude-code session, the runner oplog has `request-usage.flush` with `reason:'stop'`, `posted>0`, `failed:0` and `statuses:[]`, and Harbour's `request-usage` collection has rows for that itemId.
   - A 401 or 404 in `statuses` means wrong.
   - **Rollback:** revert the PR's merge commit. Do not use `SD_WORKER_USAGE_RELAY=0` as the safe flag, because it also stops snapshots. Stored records are additive and nothing reads them until piece 4.
3. **Cancel or abort posts land while the row is taken.** **Inside** (D10c). I confirmed it from code on the Harbour side (above); no end-to-end run.
   - Settle **after the deploy**. The first manual abort of a running claude-code session logs `request-usage.flush` with `reason:'cancel'` and no 404 in `statuses`.
4. **Tail coverage after Stop is reap-only.** The terminal flush runs only for COMPLETED sessions with `closeOnDone` armed. It does not run when `[done]` failed to propagate (closeOnDone deliberately not armed) or when `SD_CLOSE_WINDOW_ON_DONE=0`. Held sessions get their tail at the next Stop. **Inside** (D10b).
   - Settle **after the deploy** with piece 3's live comparison (LIN-4200, which gates the read switch). Records below snapshots on sessions whose done post failed shows the gap.
   - Without that comparison no check short of production shows the frequency.
5. **A permanent 400 is retried on every flush.** **Outside**: the ticket's retry rule names 5xx, timeout and 404, and the runner never builds a body the intake would 400. No action. It is visible as `400` in the oplog `statuses`.
6. **404 reading.** The ticket's constraint (retry on the next flush) governs over the LIN-4198 note (stop retrying). The code follows the ticket. A repost is `$max`-idempotent, and a terminal session has no further flush, so the conflict costs nothing. **Inside**; discharged.
7. **The ledger is never pruned in `state/sessions.json`.** It is about 30 bytes per request id, kept until the 7-day record pass. Review note 6 allowed the short-hash form, so this meets the requirement. **Outside**: if the file's size or rewrite cost becomes visible, that is its own ticket.
8. **Doc fix for close-out.** `docs/module-map.md:322` says the flush posts to `/api/proxy/runner/usage/:id`. It should say "`/api/dispatch/usage/:itemId` with the workspace dispatch token". **Inside**: this change's own doc.

### Verdict
Approve — conditional on close-out discharging the ledger.

The walk, ledger, resend and all seams are correct and mutation-proven, and snapshot posting is unchanged. Before merging, close-out must:
- make the workflow sub-agent walk fix (item 1) with its witness;
- correct the doc (item 8);
- re-check CI on the new head;
- note the plan correction on LIN-4195.

Items 2–4 are post-deploy steps.

## Close-out — LIN-4199

**Merged:** https://github.com/JKershaw/simple-dispatcher/pull/314, squash commit `9478e1c534279e7877750d8032798ac35b92b883`, pinned with `--match-head-commit f2dc0af`. Review verdict was Approve, conditional on the ledger below.

### Changes I made after the approval (nobody else reviewed these)
- `f2dc0af` — **Review ledger item 1** (workflow subagent transcripts). `subagentSources` in `request-usage-flush.js` now also reads `subagents/workflows/wf_*/agent-*.jsonl`. Order: top-level files first, then workflow directories, every level sorted; `agent` is the file's basename; `journal.jsonl` and `*.meta.json` are not read. New witness (g2) in `test/request-usage-stop.test.js`: an id only in `wf_x/agent-b.jsonl` posts with `agent:'agent-b'`, an id shared with the main file posts once at the per-field max, and a decoy `journal.jsonl` / `agent-b.meta.json` is not read. Mutation check: with the workflow read removed the witness fails (1 of 7 in the file); restored, it passes.
- `f2dc0af` — stale comment: `transcript.js:432` now names both subagent locations.
- `f2dc0af` — **Review ledger item 8** (doc): `docs/module-map.md` now says the flush posts to `/api/dispatch/usage/:itemId` with the workspace dispatch token (and mentions the workflow walk).
- No other file or assertion changed.

### CI
CI exists (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`). `unit tests` was SUCCESS on the exact head `f2dc0af` (run 41776248737) before the merge. Local full suite on the same head: 3962 tests, 3957 pass, 0 fail, 5 skipped.

### Ledger
1. Workflow subagent transcripts — **inside, done** (above, `f2dc0af`).
2. Live intake acceptance — **inside, mostly verified after the deploy.** The live runner checkout is at `9478e1c` and its first Stop after the merge logged `request-usage.flush` with `reason:'stop'`, `records:136`, `posted:136`, `failed:0`, `statuses:[]`, `rejected:0` (oplog `2026-11-04T05:00:09Z`, session `9ca63857…`, item `f6248f11…` = LIN-4202). Only a 200 enters the ledger, and the session's `requestLedger` holds 136 entries, so the intake answered 200. **Not run:** reading Harbour's `request-usage` collection for that item. No endpoint reads the collection until piece 4, and I have no production DB access. Whoever has it can run `db['request-usage'].countDocuments({itemId:'f6248f11-a05e-49c3-a001-6f1040592392'})` and expect ~136.
3. Cancel/abort posts land while the row is taken — **inside, check not run.** Needs a manual abort of a running claude-code session, which I will not trigger on someone else's work. What to look for: `request-usage.flush` with `reason:'cancel'` and no `404` in `statuses`. Code proof stands (review: `readTakenForUsage` filters `status:'taken'`, a cancelled taken row stays `taken`).
4. Tail coverage after Stop is reap-only — **inside, check not run.** Settles with LIN-4200's live comparison (records vs snapshots), which needs real elapsed time and is already its own ticket. Not a monitor; nothing fires.
5. Permanent 400 retried every flush — **outside, no action** per review (visible as `400` in oplog `statuses`; the runner never builds a body the intake would 400).
6. 404 reading — **inside, discharged.** The ticket's rule (retry at the next flush) governs; the code follows it; a repost is `$max`-idempotent.
7. Ledger never pruned in `sessions.json` — **outside, filed as LIN-4204** (priority Low: gradual size/rewrite-cost risk, no measured problem; labels Improvement, kind:follow-up, front:cost-economy; related to this ticket). Existing-ticket search found no ticket naming the request ledger.
8. Doc fix — **inside, done** (`f2dc0af`).
- Plan correction noted on LIN-4195.

**Rollback (named by review):** revert merge commit `9478e1c`. Do not use `SD_WORKER_USAGE_RELAY=0`: it also stops snapshots. Stored records are additive and nothing reads them until piece 4.

### Not run (for the operator)
- Harbour-side row count for item `f6248f11…` (needs production DB access).
- First manual abort of a running claude-code session (`reason:'cancel'`, no 404).
- Piece 3 (LIN-4200) comparison for sessions whose `[done]` post failed.

### Housekeeping
Description archived first (snapshot `4b3de435…`, verified to equal the pre-close description). Nothing in it was a discharged stage artifact (the plan is on LIN-4195), so only an implemented stub was appended; the spec and acceptance are untouched. LIN-4200 (piece 3) is unblocked by this merge and stays Todo. LIN-4195 and the other siblings are unchanged.

## Survey 1a (round 3)

**1. Why it was difficult.** The walk and the ledger were easy: piece 0's corpus pinned them. The hard part was the flush points. "Terminal-session reap" sounded like one seam. In practice terminal phases are written inline in about six places: the hook's `complete`/`failed`, `applyAbortEffects`, the forced-resume cancel, `failSession`, the stall failsafe's `fail` arm, and the done-window reap. I wired the obvious one first and had to be pushed to enumerate the rest. Three contracts also had to be worked around:
- the synchronous "no await" rule in `applyAbortEffects`, which forced detached flushes;
- the Stop-hook time budget, which forced a deadline and a feedback reserve;
- `state-store` capturing `SD_STATE_FILE` at require time, which meant changing the shared test driver.

Two environmental surprises cost time. The leak trap caught a pre-existing shared-`/tmp` fixture that my flush started reading. CI on Linux drained an event loop that macOS did not, because `fetchWithTimeout` unrefs its timer.

**2. What I'd do first.** Grep every terminal-phase write and verify the intake's route and auth against Harbour's code, all before writing a witness. Both corrections (the dispatch route rather than the runner twin, and the full set of transitions) came late and forced rework.

**3. What I'd tidy.**
- One `transitionToTerminal(sid, phase, reason)` in `phases.js` or `state-store`, with the flush hooked there, in place of six call sites that each have to remember it.
- Fold the six `request-usage-*` test files into two: pure, and seams.
- Make `REQUEST_USAGE_FEEDBACK_RESERVE_MS` configurable rather than a literal.
- Decide what a permanent 400 should do; today it retries on every flush.

**4. What the ticket would be if the code were how I'd want it.** "Post records at Stop and on terminal transition," with one seam for each. The reap and cancel work would disappear into that helper. A transcript reader that knew the `subagents/` layout would have removed D11.

**5. What the ticket or plan got wrong.**
- It steered me to `/api/proxy/runner/usage` and the `take` grant. The runner's credential is a consumer dispatch token, so the right route is `/api/dispatch/usage/:itemId`, with the same token and ownership rule as feedback.
- "(b) terminal-session cleanup/reap" understated how many transitions exist.
- "Replace the seven snapshot sites with one call" doesn't fit piece 2, which keeps the snapshots. I added one pre-switch flush beside them.
- Its line references were accurate.

My own misses: I claimed red-first witnesses before I had run them red, I wrote one witness that tested nothing until I fixed it, and I made several heredoc and shell slips. All were caught before the PR.
